doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Receiving the NEA Jazz Masters Award in 1989
summary: He is surprised to have received the award in 1989, before others, and thinks it was for his teaching.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Can you just mention about your NEA Jazz Masters Award?
Oh, yeah, my NEA Jazz Masters Award…
Talk about that a little bit.
Mine came a long time ago, I was surprised at the ones that came after me. I say, “What [inaudible] should have gotten his before me, you know.”

1989. Yeah, 1989, I got mine a long way, I even saw the names somewhere. Might have been Hank Jones, I don’t know, something like that. The studio was, I got mine in 1989 and it was a good time too because, oh yeah, check ’89 in there.
Yeah, ain’t that something? Look at that, me with Hank Jones. Look who got the next year.
George Russell, Cecil Taylor, Gerald Wilson.
All them before me. And who the next year?
Danny Barker, Buck Clayton, Andy Kirk, Clark Terry.
You see, I don't know how I got mine so quick in 1989 with all those people, but I’m glad I got it though.
Ain’t that something, think about that.
1996. I got mine, well, I think it’s probably because of my teaching mostly, you know. I think that’s what it was because I’ve taught so many people, so many, you know, so many, you know.
